description: The chart illustrates average token counts across different few-shot settings by showing how many tokens are attributed to “Reasoning” versus “Demonstration” for each number of shots. The horizontal axis contains the categories “Number of Shots,” ordered from 0 through 4 in increasing order. The vertical axis is labeled “Token Count” and uses a linear scale from 0 to 7000 with regularly spaced tick marks every 1000 tokens. Each category is represented by a stacked vertical bar with an orange “Reasoning” segment and, for shots 1–4, a blue “Demonstration” segment stacked on top; the 0-shot bar is orange only and is labeled 6393 tokens. For 1 shot, the stacked bar reaches roughly 4400–4500 tokens total, with the orange portion around 4200–4300 and a small blue cap around 200–300; for 2 shots, the total is around 4700–4800 with orange near 4500 and blue near 200–300; for 3 shots, the total is around 5300–5400 with orange near 5000 and blue near 300–400; for 4 shots, the total is around 5000 with orange near 4200–4300 and a larger blue segment around 700–800. A gray dashed horizontal reference line is drawn at the zero-shot level (aligned with the 6393 label), and red downward arrows with numeric annotations (−1952, −1613, −1040, and −1379) are placed above the 1-, 2-, 3-, and 4-shot bars respectively, pointing from the dashed line down to the bar tops; no additional sorting beyond the numeric shot order is shown, and the main visual emphasis comes from the dashed reference line and red arrow annotations.
